findings.summary: README top-level status inventory is stale relative to the merged #17–#22 foundation.
exact_evidence: README.md Current Status lists accepted ADRs only through ADR 0012 and application-invalid matrices only through Issue #16.
The same README later contains Issue #17–#21 implementation sections, creating an internally inconsistent active status description.
Issue #22 is absent from the README even though its 52-scenario representative corpus is merged on the audit baseline.
findings.expected_architecture: Active status documentation must describe the complete accepted foundation through ADR 0017 and the Issue #22 integration corpus without implying that the foundation stops at Issue #16.
findings.observed_problem: The README contains both an older top-level foundation inventory and newer issue-specific sections.
findings.risk_or_consequence: An implementation agent could incorrectly treat later record families as provisional or overlook the representative graph corpus when planning runtime work.
findings.required_disposition: Reconcile the README status inventory with the merged foundation and add an Issue #22 current-implementation section.
findings.resolution: Slice 1 updates README Current Status to cover ADRs 0001–0017, contract families through Issue #21, and the Issue #22 15-positive/37-negative integration corpus.
validation_evidence: Issue #23 foundation validator checks required audit artifacts and traceability.

findings.summary: README assigns future pds-sunset suite-wide archival ownership more broadly than ADR 0017 permits.
exact_evidence: README.md sibling-module list says `pds-sunset` will own suite-wide archival orchestration.
ADR 0017 says no pds-sunset repository exists, a future Sunset-like component is orchestration-only, Portia retains semantic authority, and Portia performs/verifies mutations of Portia-owned custody.
findings.expected_architecture: A future retention/disposition orchestrator coordinates policy-fed cross-module planning and fan-out; each module retains semantic and mutation authority over its own custody.
findings.observed_problem: The README verb `own` can be read as transferring archival/destruction authority to a future module.
findings.risk_or_consequence: A later implementation could centralize destructive authority contrary to the accepted fail-closed module-side contract.
findings.required_disposition: Narrow README language to orchestration-only and preserve the absence of a current runtime dependency.
findings.resolution: Slice 1 replaces the ownership statement with the ADR 0017 orchestration-only boundary.
validation_evidence: ADR disposition/traceability records ADR 0017 as controlling.

findings.summary: README product-position language overstates Portia as recording what 'the institution decided'.
exact_evidence: README Product Position describes Portia as recording 'what the institution decided'.
The accepted teacher-local architecture requires explicit decision authority and prohibits teacher-local judgments from masquerading as institution-wide findings.
findings.expected_architecture: Portia records attributable decisions and the authority/scope under which they were made; it does not upgrade a teacher-local record into institutional truth.
findings.observed_problem: The unqualified product-position phrase is broader than the accepted authority model.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Downstream UI/reporting could present local Determinations as institutionally authoritative.
findings.required_disposition: Use authority-bounded wording in the product position.
findings.resolution: Slice 1 changes the sentence to record 'what an attributable human decided within documented authority'.

findings.summary: Final post-audit repository validation and final audited commit binding are not yet available.
exact_evidence: The #22 handoff reports 1451/1451 complete schema-validation tests on the pre-#23 baseline.
Issue #23 changes audit documentation, tests, validator code, README language, and schema documentation; the final suite must therefore be rerun in the actual checkout.
The explicit ready approval record must bind the exact final audited commit, which does not exist until the repaired worktree is validated and committed.
findings.expected_architecture: A ready verdict is issued only after the actual post-audit checkout passes the full suite and the approval record can bind the exact audited commit.
findings.observed_problem: At Slice 1 authoring time only the merged #22 baseline is available as complete-suite evidence.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Issuing approval now would make the approval record self-inconsistent and would inherit test evidence across an untested diff.
findings.required_disposition: Run the full current suite, Issue #22 regression, audit validator, and git diff --check in the user's checkout; then resolve this finding and create the approval record in a closeout slice.
validation_evidence: Pending user-local confirmation after Slice 1 application.

findings.summary: The executable milestone must implement append-preserving recovery without pretending multi-file or cross-module actions are magically atomic.
exact_evidence: ADR 0009 uses immutable journals, pointers, exact fingerprints, ordered writes, locks, and reconciliation.
ADR 0017 explicitly allows partial cross-module success and rejects reconstruction of deleted content as rollback.
findings.expected_architecture: Runtime services reconcile exact durable state and preserve accepted history.
findings.observed_problem: No executable persistence layer exists yet, so this correctness property is architectural rather than runtime-proven.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Naive rollback/retry logic could duplicate accepted records or erase accepted history.
findings.required_disposition: Carry the invariant directly into production persistence/recovery acceptance tests.
findings.resolution: Accepted as implementation guidance; no foundation change required.

findings.summary: Privacy-safe handling of free text and multi-party records requires fail-closed/manual-review paths that must not become routine technical administration for teachers.
exact_evidence: ADR 0017 requires manual review when mechanical redaction would alter proposition, attribution, evidence basis, or practical meaning.
The foundation separately requires proportionate teacher workload.
findings.expected_architecture: The runtime automates safe structural handling and surfaces concise, semantic review decisions only when required.
findings.observed_problem: The architecture deliberately leaves UI/workflow implementation to the next milestone.
findings.risk_or_consequence: A literal low-level implementation could force teachers to manage field policies, identifiers, provenance, or redaction mechanics directly.
findings.required_disposition: Design later workflows around concise review decisions while keeping low-level policy/provenance generation automatic.

findings.summary: Issue #22 proves application invariants through a test-only graph validator; production runtime validation still has to be implemented.
exact_evidence: tests/schema_validation/issue_22_graph_validation.py is explicitly a test-only integration validator.
37 individually schema-valid graphs are intentionally rejected only at application-validation level.
findings.expected_architecture: The executable milestone must enforce the same exact-reference, ownership, lifecycle, provenance, recovery, privacy, and custody invariants at runtime boundaries.
findings.observed_problem: There is intentionally no executable Portia application in the foundation milestone.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Treating JSON Schema as sufficient would admit graphs the foundation has already defined as invalid.
findings.required_disposition: Translate the stable graph invariants into production validation/services without making the test helper a runtime API by accident.
validation_evidence: Schema/application separation documented throughout the foundation.

findings.summary: Retention periods, legal holds, requester entitlement, disclosure authorization, and destruction approval remain external policy decisions.
exact_evidence: ADR 0017 deliberately defines semantic retention classes and policy hooks rather than legal durations.
Portia cannot prove guardianship, entitlement, legal-hold state, institution destruction approval, or purge of external copies.
findings.expected_architecture: Portia accepts bounded externally authoritative inputs and fails closed when required policy facts are unavailable.
findings.observed_problem: No generic local-first module can infer institution- and jurisdiction-specific policy truth from the record graph alone.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Hard-coded legal assumptions would create false authority and unsafe deletion/disclosure behavior.
findings.required_disposition: Preserve external policy provenance and blocked/unresolved states in future runtime work.
findings.resolution: Accepted policy dependency; not a Portia foundation defect.

findings.summary: The shared Sunset-like adapter protocol remains intentionally undefined.
exact_evidence: ADR 0017 defines conceptual Portia capabilities but publishes no premature shared protocol.
At the audited checkpoint no pds-sunset repository is required by Portia.
findings.expected_architecture: A future suite-level protocol can negotiate capabilities while preserving module-local semantics and mutation authority.
findings.observed_problem: There is no accepted suite protocol yet.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Premature Portia-only wire contracts would likely create cross-module coupling and protocol drift.
findings.required_disposition: Define the shared protocol only when the suite is ready to design the orchestrator.

findings.summary: A privacy-minimized Core intervention publication projection remains future integration work.
exact_evidence: ADR 0014/README preserve Portia-native support/intervention authority and identify Core v0.6 intervention_record_set only as a future projection.
Issue #18 explicitly does not create academic registration, results, Grades, automatic Meridian publication, or automatic portfolio publication.
findings.expected_architecture: Any future publication remains consumer-neutral and privacy-minimized while Portia stays authoritative for native records.
findings.observed_problem: No live producer projection is required by the foundation milestone.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Implementing publication prematurely could leak behavior/support detail or conflate behavior support with academic evidence.
findings.required_disposition: Defer until an explicit integration issue defines the projection and authorization policy.
findings.follow_up_issue_if_any: Future Core intervention publication integration issue

findings.summary: A working Portia application, production persistence services, GUI/CLI workflows, and live sibling adapters are deliberately outside the foundations milestone.
exact_evidence: Umbrella #10 explicitly states that the completed foundation does not require a working Portia application.
Current README likewise identifies production filesystem services and teacher-facing workflows as later executable work.
findings.expected_architecture: The foundation must constrain later implementation without pretending the runtime already exists.
findings.risk_or_consequence: Treating runtime absence as a blocker would expand #23 into a different milestone; treating architecture as runtime proof would be equally incorrect.
findings.required_disposition: Preserve the non-goal while carrying audit constraints into the executable milestone.

findings.summary: The foundation audit does not certify FERPA, state-law, district-policy, clinical, special-education, or records-management compliance.
exact_evidence: ADR 0017 treats legal entitlement, policy interpretation, legal holds, and destruction authorization as institution/deployment responsibilities.
Portia explicitly rejects institutional discipline, clinical, IEP, threat-assessment, and district case-management scope.
findings.expected_architecture: Portia exposes truthful boundaries and policy hooks without claiming legal conclusions it cannot establish.
findings.observed_problem: Compliance depends on deployment context and institutional policy beyond the repository.
findings.risk_or_consequence: A foundation-approval record could be misread as legal certification if the non-claim is not explicit.
findings.required_disposition: State the non-claim prominently in audit and approval documentation.

findings.summary: Issue #22 exact-byte fixture evidence is not checkout-portable because the repository does not pin text files to LF.
exact_evidence: The first Windows post-audit full-suite run executed 1466 tests and reported 24 failures.
The exact-byte failures show byte-length deltas equal to inserted carriage-return counts, including 1051→1089, 581→600, 1825→1897, and 558→577.
Failures span P22-06 import provenance, P22-12 privacy/export provenance, P22-13 derived snapshots, P22-14 coordinated-operation recovery, and G22-032/G22-033 privacy negatives.
Git reports the affected fixture files clean because line-ending normalization can materialize CRLF in the working tree while the index retains LF.
No .gitattributes file exists on the Issue #22 baseline.
findings.expected_architecture: Exact-byte provenance and recovery fixtures must materialize identically on supported developer platforms; repository checkout policy must preserve the LF bytes against which the accepted SHA-256 and byte-length evidence was computed.
findings.observed_problem: On a normal Windows checkout, text fixtures can be materialized as CRLF. Their semantic JSON/text content is unchanged, but exact bytes no longer match the accepted fingerprints, causing valid positive graphs to fail and negative graphs to acquire unrelated fingerprint findings.
findings.risk_or_consequence: The foundation's exact-byte provenance tests become platform-dependent. A Windows implementation agent can receive a clean Git tree that nevertheless fails the canonical recovery/privacy/import evidence, obscuring genuine integrity defects behind checkout behavior.
findings.required_disposition: Pin repository text checkout to LF with .gitattributes, re-materialize the current Issue #22 fixture working tree from the accepted HEAD blobs under that policy, and make the Issue #23 validator reject missing LF policy or CRLF materialization inside the exact-byte corpus.
findings.resolution: Slices 2–3 add a repository LF checkout policy, re-materialize Issue #22 fixtures from the accepted HEAD blobs instead of editing the historical corpus, make the Issue #23 temporary fixture writer emit LF explicitly on every platform, and extend the audit validator/regression tests so this portability invariant cannot silently regress.
validation_evidence: First user-local post-audit full-suite run: Ran 1466 tests; FAILED (failures=24).
Observed fingerprint byte-length deltas have the exact CRLF signature.
Second user-local rerun after Slice 2: Ran 1469 tests; FAILED (failures=6); the broad Issue #22 fingerprint cluster was removed.
The remaining visible Issue #23 validator failure was caused by its own platform-native Path.write_text temporary fixture writer.
Issue #23 validator requires '* text=auto eol=lf' and rejects CRLF in Issue #22 text fixtures.
Slice 3 restores tests/fixtures/issue_22 from HEAD after installing .gitattributes and uses explicit LF writes in the focused validator tests.
Third user-local rerun after Slice 3: Ran 1470 tests; FAILED (failures=5).
No tests/fixtures/issue_22 paths were reported modified after Slice 3, confirming the raw-HEAD LF re-materialization removed the corpus-wide working-tree rewrite.

All five remaining failures are historical README compatibility assertions: the Issue #12/#13 checkpoint phrase 'Architecture Decision Records through ADR 0009', the Issue #14 checkpoint phrases 'Architecture Decision Records through ADR 0009' and 'Actor Directory version-1 record family', and the Issue #16 phrase 'accepted ADR 0012 for Review'.
Slice 4 restores those exact strings as explicitly historical checkpoint language while preserving ADRs 0001–0017 and the current schema catalog as present authority.
